meta.description: Muller Records — Frank Müller's Berlin techno label since 1996. Catalogue, roster, history and merchandise.

artists.label: Roster
artists.title: Who has released here
artists.body: Detroit, Tokyo, Grenoble, New York, Berlin. The label never had a house sound so much as a standard — records that work at 3am and still hold up on headphones the next afternoon.

story.label: History
story.quote: Started in a Berlin that was still deciding what it was going to be.
story.bodyOne: Frank Müller moved to Berlin in 1992, a trained mechanical engineer who had been DJing since the mid-eighties. Acid Orange followed in 1993 and ran twenty records deep, including Toktok's debut single. Muller Records opened in 1996.
story.bodyTwo: What followed was thirty years of records that refused to pick a lane: Detroit techno, acid, new wave melody, and a permanent open line to Tokyo, where Beroshima plays to rooms most European producers never see.
story.portraitAlt: Frank Müller as Beroshima, in sunglasses and a red jacket, lit from behind

merch.label: Merch
merch.title: The mark on cotton
merch.body: The logo has outlasted most of the clubs it was played in. Shirts, hoodies, slipmats and record bundles — built around the mark, not printed over it.

artists.label: Roster
artists.title: Artists
artists.lede: {count} names have put a record or a remix out on a Muller imprint. Some of them define whole cities of this music.
artists.heroPhotoAlt: Takkyu Ishino standing in a club, mirrorball light across the room behind him
artists.orderNote: In the label's own order, running roughly through the catalogue's history rather than the alphabet.

catalog.label: Catalogue
catalog.title: Catalogue
catalog.lede: Every release documented so far, grouped by imprint and running newest first.
catalog.disclaimer: This listing is compiled from public sources and is not yet complete — the pre-2000 records in particular are still being entered. The definitive discography lives on

history.label: History
history.title: History & impact
history.lede: Thirty years of a Berlin label, told through the records that changed what it was.
history.heroPhotoAlt: Sleeve of Beroshima's The Catastrophe Ballet: a man kneeling on a beach, vacuuming the sand

photos.tapeAlt: Frank Müller at a reel-to-reel tape machine, in a suit and tie
photos.wallAlt: Frank Müller shielding his eyes, standing in front of a wall of records

dj.title: First records, first rooms
dj.body: Frank Müller starts DJing in the mid-eighties, years before techno had a name in Germany. The training is mechanical engineering; the education is new wave and early electronics.

berlin.title: Berlin
berlin.body: After several years in the Netherlands, Müller moves to Berlin in 1992 — into a city where the techno scene is being built in real time out of the buildings nobody wanted.

acidOrange.title: Acid Orange
acidOrange.body: The first label. Twenty releases over its run, and a catalogue that establishes the acid streak still audible in everything Müller puts out.

toktok.title: Toktok's debut
toktok.body: Acid Orange releases the first Toktok single — one of several instances of the label being where an artist starts rather than where they arrive.

muller.title: Muller Records
muller.body: The main line opens in Berlin. Over the following years it releases Claude Young, John Selway, The Hacker, Air Liquide, Rok, Autotune and Latex, and becomes a fixed part of the city's scene rather than a passing imprint.

matadors.title: Matadors Of Techno
matadors.body: Beroshima and Takkyu Ishino of Denki Groove record together — the clearest single marker of the Berlin–Tokyo line that runs through the label's whole history.

beroshimaMusic.title: Beroshima Music, and POP
beroshimaMusic.body: Müller opens an imprint for his own work and releases the debut album POP · Pornography Of Performance. Beroshima stops being a project name and becomes a body of work.

ballet.title: The Catastrophe Ballet
ballet.body: The second album. New wave melody carried on techno structure — the combination that keeps the catalogue recognisable across decades.

cocoon.title: Horizon on Cocoon
cocoon.body: Sven Väth's Cocoon Recordings releases Horizon. The remix package pulls in Tigerskin, Ulrich Schnauss, Funk D'Void and Pig & Dan, and the track travels far past the label's own reach.

polyphonication.title: Polyphonication
polyphonication.body: A studio album deep into the label's second decade, at a point when most of the imprints that started in 1996 have long since stopped.

madMusician.title: Mad Musician
madMusician.body: A new series, numbered from one, with Ken Ishii, Kirk Degiorgio and Donna Summer on the credits. The vault reopens and the label keeps pressing.

berlin.title: Part of the Berlin furniture
berlin.body: Founded in 1996 and never sold, never folded, never rebranded. Berlin has cycled through several complete generations of labels in that time. Muller Records is one of the constants.

japan.title: The Tokyo line
japan.body: Frank Müller aka Beroshima holds a standing in Japan few European techno producers reach, with releases and collaborations running through Ken Ishii and Takkyu Ishino. The label's catalogue carries Japanese artists as a matter of course, not as an exotic detour.

detroit.title: Detroit, properly
detroit.body: Claude Young, John Selway and Kirk Degiorgio on the catalogue is not decoration. The label earned its Detroit connections by releasing those records at the time, not by citing them afterwards.

longevity.title: A catalogue, not a moment
longevity.body: Over a hundred documented releases across four imprints, from 12" vinyl to digital, spanning the entire arc from the mid-nineties rave economy to streaming. Very few independent techno labels have a run that long.

sources.title: Sources
sources.body: The history above is compiled from public documentation. Corrections from the label take precedence over all of it.

merch.label: Merch
merch.title: Merch
merch.lede: Shirts and records, straight from the label's own Bandcamp store. Every buy button goes there — no second checkout, no third-party print farm.
merch.heroPhotoAlt: Beroshima behind the decks in a dark club, light trails across the mixer

apparel.title: Shirts
apparel.body: Silver print, two colourways. Pick a cut and a size — each one is its own listing, and a size crossed out is a size that is gone.

vinyl.title: Records in stock
vinyl.body: Vinyl and CDs still available, including test pressings and coloured runs. Prices and stock come from Bandcamp, so what you see here is what is actually left.

gone.title: Out of print
gone.body: Pressed, sold, gone. Listed because a catalogue that sold out is part of the record too — try the second-hand market.

records.title: Records first
records.body: The merch exists because the records do. Everything in the catalogue that is still available sits on Bandcamp — digital, and vinyl while stock lasts.

wholesale.title: Stores & wholesale
wholesale.body: Record shops and distributors: get in touch directly for wholesale terms on merch and back catalogue.

contact.label: Contact
contact.title: Contact
contact.lede: Demos, bookings, press. One address, read by the label.
contact.heroPhotoAlt: Frank Müller mixing, headphones round his neck, hands on the mixer

demos.title: Demos
demos.body: Send a private streaming link rather than attachments. Two or three tracks is enough. No reply within a month means it was not a fit this time.

bookings.title: Bookings
bookings.body: Beroshima live and DJ bookings. Include date, city, venue capacity and the rest of the line-up.

press.title: Press & licensing
press.body: Interviews, press assets, sync and licensing requests for the catalogue.

footer.blurb: Muller Records is the Berlin label founded by Frank Müller — Beroshima — in 1996, alongside Acid Orange, Beroshima Music and the Mad Musician series.
